review.summary: Attempt 2 fixes most of attempt 1's findings. Two new receipts record the delivery verifier actually running: `execution-main.json` on `main`, and `execution-release-tree.json` inside this tree with `--root .`. Both report 11/11 tests passing and `verify` returning `delivered`. Four negative tests were added. Release-readiness attempt 4 (44/50, accepted) is bound to the published `f9cebee5…`. Stale notes and the `active_followup_plan` mismatch are now explained. The registry, tag, branch and CI-44 receipts (49/49 success, no non-success statuses) agree with each other and with the `PHASES.md` acceptance text. What remains: the recorded 105-command gate (same checks file and sha as attempt 1) still does not run the verifier. The execution receipts are self-reported, not produced by the gate. The archive comparison still depends on a gitignored archive. The `--root` handling in the copied tool is fragile.

findings.description: The execution receipts are the only proof the verifier ran. They are hand-assembled JSON: nothing in the repo produces them, and they are not part of `docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-remote-delivery-attempt-02.checks.json`. That checks file has the same sha256 (90ef8077…) as attempt 1 and contains 105 commands, none of them historical_delivery. The receipts also depend on the gitignored `.local/artifacts` crate, so a reviewer cannot reproduce the archive-bytes step offline. `tests.path` is a bare `test_historical_delivery.py` instead of a repo-relative path.
findings.required_fix: Commit the script that produced the receipts, or reference the commit and blob sha of that script on main. Record repo-relative test paths (`docs/reviews/historical-delivery/test_historical_delivery.py`). Have the phase-completion step on `main` re-run `verify --version 0.2.4` and the tests as recorded checks bound to source and checks sha256.

findings.description: `_root` finds `--root` by scanning `sys.argv` when the module is imported. `main()` parses `--root` but never uses `args.root` (lines 332-335). So `--root=.` or a programmatic `main([...,'--root','.'])` silently falls back to `parents[1]`, which is `docs/reviews` for the copy. The `release_delivery` import then fails or resolves against the wrong tree.
findings.required_fix: Resolve ROOT from the parsed `args.root` inside `main()` and import `release_delivery` lazily from that root, or reject `--root=` forms explicitly.

findings.description: The superseded, unbound transcription is still in the evidence directory. It has the same status and shape as a real result, and only the prose in `phase-28-historical-delivery.md:87-89` marks it as superseded.
findings.required_fix: Add a `supersededBy` field pointing to the two execution receipts, or remove the file in an evidence-only commit.

findings.description: There is a stray extra blank line between test methods. No test calls `main()` or the `--root` path, which is the code the release-tree receipt actually relied on.
findings.required_fix: Add a test that runs `main(['verify','--version','0.2.4','--root',str(root)])` against the temp repo, and fix the blank line.

evidence: Checks file: passed=true, source f9cebee5…, 105 commands, and grep finds no non-zero exit_code or timeout. The sha256 90ef8077… matches attempt 1 (`phase-28-chunk-remote-delivery-attempt-01.json:8`).

`execution-release-tree.json:5-41`: headCommit dba8caf, clean tree, tool sha 73c05267…, tests exit 0 ('Ran 11 tests'), `verify --root .` returns status 'delivered', ciRun 44, 49 jobs, `failedContexts` [].
`execution-main.json:5-41`: headCommit e229c13, same tool and test sha256s, same result.

`test_historical_delivery.py:180-224`: new tests cover a stray proof commit, a proof naming a different fingerprint, registry yanked/owner/version/source changes, and manifest identity. This resolves prior low finding #6.
`phase-28-chunk-release-readiness-attempt-04.json:6,11,66,70`: source f9cebee5…, gate_passed true, total 44, accepted. This resolves prior medium finding #3.
`phase-28-published-archive-comparison.json:35` and `phase-28-historical-delivery.md:32-35`: post-publication regeneration disclosed. Resolves prior low finding #4.
`phase-28-historical-delivery.md:103-107` explains the legacy `active_followup_plan` (`phase-status.json:8698`). Resolves prior low finding #5.
`ci-run-44.json:4-10`: run 44 success on 7dd0fff with fingerprint f9cebee5…; grep finds 0 failure/cancelled/pending/skipped statuses.
`historical_delivery.py:239-323` checks registry identity, archive inventory, proof fingerprint and ancestry, tag peeling, CI matrix completeness and exceptions.
`PHASES.md:299-303`: remote-delivery acceptance (registry bytes, annotated tag, 49 terminal successes) is matched by the receipts.
limitations: Read-only review with no network access and no commands run, so I did not compute sha256 values. I compared the tool and test hashes in the receipts with each other but not with the files on disk.
The retained crates.io archive under `.local/artifacts` is gitignored and was not inspected. Byte equality rests on the execution receipts and the committed file inventories.
I did not inspect `main`'s `tools/historical_delivery.py` or `main`'s copy of the readiness attempt-4 artifacts.
Fingerprinted release source (SDK code, `tools/check_phase.py`, `release_delivery.py`) is unchanged since 0.2.4, so I did not re-audit it.
